representations.name: signed prime-exponent circuit hypergraph
representations.new_information: keeps the exact {-1,0,1} coefficient restriction, the support of each minimal unbalanced relation, and the cardinality imbalance as a signed circuit label
representations.first_test: generate every minimal bad support through N=18 and compare it with the repeated-factor integer-kernel circuits

representations.name: affine lift by the cardinality coordinate
representations.new_information: compares subset sums of v(n) and (v(n),1), so the defect is exactly a projection collision between different 0/1 Hamming layers rather than arbitrary linear dependence
representations.first_test: use {2,4} and long bipartite edge-prime circuits to reject any lift that silently allows coefficients outside {-1,0,1}

representations.name: prime-labelled bipartite incidence realization
representations.new_information: realizes squarefree product relations as connected bipartite incidence graphs whose edge primes certify equality and whose shore imbalance records the forbidden cardinality difference
representations.first_test: construct K_(s+1,s) for arbitrary s and verify equality, distinctness, minimality, and high-tail placement symbolically

representations.name: nonlinear auxiliary-element supply hypergraph
representations.new_information: separates a formal polarization identity from the density theorem needed to place all auxiliary multiples or products inside one candidate set
representations.first_test: test (2x)(2y)=4xy against high-tail density-one finite sets and measure which sparse auxiliary locus can be deleted for free

representations.name: logarithmic high-tail filtration
representations.new_information: converts a cardinality imbalance into a strict product-size gap for all relations up to a moving length L(N), while recording exactly where long circuits escape
representations.first_test: prove the N^(1-1/L) cutoff lemma and insert K_(s+1,s) circuits with s>=L

representations.name: large-prime fibre peeling
representations.new_information: orders primes above a smoothness cutoff, retains their exact incidence and exponents in a minimal circuit, and exposes prime fibres that must balance across the two shores
representations.first_test: split at y=N^(1/L), remove the y-smooth core, and classify how K_(s+1,s) circuits defeat naive private-prime peeling

representations.name: bounded-prime-dimension lattice obstruction
representations.new_information: tracks exponent height as well as prime dimension, distinguishing rational dependence from a forbidden binary affine collision
representations.first_test: compare one-dimensional superincreasing exponent sets with dense lattice boxes before claiming a dimension-only bound

representations.name: private-prime matching and Hall deficiency
representations.new_information: records whether admitted integers can receive distinct prime certificates and localizes the exact deficiency when prime labels must be reused
representations.first_test: apply Hall counting on [N] and reject any density-one claim that assigns at most one integer to each of pi(N) primes

representations.name: minimal-relation hitting-set ILP
representations.new_information: gives a complete fixed-N formulation with one binary admission variable per integer and one inequality per inclusion-minimal bad support
representations.first_test: enumerate exact subset products and reproduce maximum admissible sizes through N=18 with an independent predicate replay

representations.name: SAT motif extraction and symbolic completeness
representations.new_information: stores prime-incidence isomorphism types, shore imbalance, circuit length, and scale so finite certificates can be tested for a genuine all-N completeness theorem
representations.first_test: ask whether every minimal bad support contains a bounded motif; use arbitrary K_(s+1,s) and unequal-shore incidence graphs as adversarial families

representations.name: periodic/profinite cylinder admission
representations.new_information: builds genuine natural-density sets from finitely many valuation conditions and makes the loss of cross-cylinder product relations explicit
representations.first_test: compute the exact density of additive level cylinders and prove the 1/e ceiling before adding any moving modulus

representations.name: finite-block gluing with multiplicative markers
representations.new_information: separates within-block admissibility from cross-block relations and measures the density price of marker primes intended to isolate blocks
representations.first_test: replay individually admissible {2,3} and {6}, whose union is bad, then quantify the loss from assigning private marker primes
